outline_section.section_title: Introduction to Converting Graphs into Unit Step Expressions
outline_section.learning_goal: Establish the minimum set of graph-reading actions needed to rewrite a signal graph as a sum of shifted unit-step windows.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A clean continuous-time graph with labeled time axis, a single nonzero interval, and highlighted breakpoints a and b.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use clean axes, high contrast strokes, and only essential labels for breakpoints and segment value.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Introduce the conversion pipeline: read all breakpoints from the graph, map each active interval to a difference of two shifted steps, and attach the interval formula to each gated term.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use one pulse example with $x(t)=A$ on $0\le t<T$ and $x(t)=0$ elsewhere to show $x(t)=A\,\big(u(t)-u(t-T)\big)$.
paragraph_plan: Define graph-to-window translation and why interval boundaries are the main objects to identify.
Introduce the base rule for a finite interval using two shifted unit steps.
Explain how segment formulas multiply the window term.
Preview the sequence: first parse intervals, then convert single segments, then combine and simplify.

solution_step_plan: N/A for tutorial section.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep this section tightly focused on the core conversion method so students build a stable schema before solving any example conversions.

outline_section.section_title: Identifying Breakpoints and Interval Formulas from a Graph
outline_section.learning_goal: Given a graph, extract an ordered breakpoint list and corresponding interval formulas before writing step terms.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A graph with alternating zero and nonzero pieces, including negative and positive breakpoints and piecewise values.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use the same visual style as the tutorial image so learners transfer the parsing routine directly.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given this graph, choose the correct ordered list of breakpoints and interval formulas.
distractor_plan: Swap adjacent breakpoints and change interval order.
Use only every other interval and collapse others.
Ignore continuity conventions at endpoint transitions.
Misread negative-time segments as all positive-time.
Omit one interval that returns to zero

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Read the displayed graph and write the interval formula table $\{(t_0,t_1]: f_1,\ (t_1,t_2]:f_2,\dots\}$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce a complete, ordered interval map that preserves values and boundaries for future conversion.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Extends the base case by handling multiple nonzero zones and negative-time regions.
solution_step_plan: Mark every breakpoint in increasing time order.
Assign the graph value formula to each open interval between neighboring breakpoints.
Check endpoint handling at each breakpoint and note if value is included or excluded.
Return the interval table as ordered data for conversion.
practice_variation_axes: Mixtures of zero and nonzero intervals

outline_section.handoff_notes: This section is data extraction only; avoid introducing step algebra yet.

prompt_blocks.text: Use the graph below. Which ordered breakpoint list and interval formulas match it?

choice_blocks.text: Breakpoints $-3,-1,2,4$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-3$, $1$ for $-3\le t<-1$, $-2$ for $-1\le t<2$, $3$ for $2\le t<4$, and $0$ for $t\ge 4$.
Breakpoints $-3,-1,2,4$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-3$, $-2$ for $-3\le t<-1$, $1$ for $-1\le t<2$, $3$ for $2\le t<4$, and $0$ for $t\ge 4$.
Breakpoints $-3,-1,4$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-3$, $1$ for $-3\le t<-1$, $3$ for $-1\le t<4$, and $0$ for $t\ge 4$.
Breakpoints $1,2,3,4$; intervals: $0$ for $t<1$, $1$ for $1\le t<2$, $-2$ for $2\le t<3$, $3$ for $3\le t<4$, and $0$ for $t\ge 4$.
Breakpoints $-3,-1,2,4$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-3$, $1$ for $-3<t\le -1$, $-2$ for $-1<t\le 2$, $3$ for $2<t\le 4$, and $0$ for $t>4$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Read the breakpoints from left to right and keep the interval values attached to the regions between them. The graph changes at $t=-3,-1,2,4$, so there are five intervals, including the leading and trailing zero regions.

prompt_blocks.text: Use the graph below. Which ordered breakpoint list and interval formulas match it?

choice_blocks.text: Breakpoints $-4,-1,2,5$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-4$, $2$ for $-4\le t<-1$, $0$ for $-1\le t<2$, $-1$ for $2\le t<5$, and $0$ for $t\ge 5$.
Breakpoints $-4,-1,2,5$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-4$, $2$ for $-4\le t<2$, $-1$ for $2\le t<5$, and $0$ for $t\ge 5$.
Breakpoints $-4,-1,5$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-4$, $2$ for $-4\le t<-1$, $-1$ for $-1\le t<5$, and $0$ for $t\ge 5$.
Breakpoints $1,4,6,9$; intervals: $0$ for $t<1$, $2$ for $1\le t<4$, $0$ for $4\le t<6$, $-1$ for $6\le t<9$, and $0$ for $t\ge 9$.
Breakpoints $-4,-1,2,5$; intervals: $0$ for $t<-4$, $2$ for $-4<t\le -1$, $0$ for $-1<t\le 2$, $-1$ for $2<t\le 5$, and $0$ for $t>5$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The middle interval is zero, but it still has its own breakpoints and must stay in the ordered list. Read every change point in increasing time order, then assign the level on each interval without collapsing the zero region.

outline_section.section_title: Converting a Single Nonzero Graph Segment into a Step Window Term
outline_section.learning_goal: Convert one isolated nonzero interval into the canonical shifted-window form $A(u(t-a)-u(t-b))$.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Graph with one isolated nonzero segment: $x(t)=A$ on $a\le t < b$, zero elsewhere.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Show only one active segment so the gate-rule $u(t-a)-u(t-b)$ is unmistakable.

question_policy.practice_question_model: From the graph, select the correct single-window conversion expression.
distractor_plan: Reverse step order to $u(t-b)-u(t-a)$.
Use only one step $A u(t-a)$.
Shift both breakpoints by the wrong sign.
Drop amplitude and write unit height.
Use $u(t-b)-u(t-a)$ with the same symbols.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Convert the graph with $x(t)=A$ for $a\le t<b$ and $x(t)=0$ elsewhere into a step form.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Create the exact gated expression and verify it turns on at $t=a$ and off at $t=b$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This adds conversion of a concrete isolated segment after interval extraction.
solution_step_plan: Read interval endpoints $a$ and $b$ from the graph.
Write base gate $u(t-a)-u(t-b)$.
Multiply gate by segment amplitude $A$.
Test representative times outside and inside the interval.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep this as a single-term conversion so learners trust the window-difference template.

prompt_blocks.text: From the graph, select the correct single-window conversion expression.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The graph is $4$ on the interval from $-2$ to $1$ and zero elsewhere, so the gate is $u(t+2)-u(t-1)$. Multiplying by the amplitude gives $4(u(t+2)-u(t-1))$.

images.image_description: A clean continuous-time graph with a labeled time axis, breakpoint markers at 1, 3, 5, and 7, a constant plateau of height 2 from 1 to 3, a constant plateau of height -1 from 3 to 5 drawn below the axis to emphasize the negative level, a constant plateau of height 3 from 5 to 7, and zero elsewhere so the three-window sum is visually obvious.

image_slot.image_description: A clean continuous-time graph with a labeled time axis, breakpoint markers at 1, 3, 5, and 7, a constant plateau of height 2 from 1 to 3, a constant plateau of height -1 from 3 to 5 drawn below the axis to emphasize the negative level, a constant plateau of height 3 from 5 to 7, and zero elsewhere so the three-window sum is visually obvious.

outline_section.section_title: Converting a Piecewise Constant Graph into Shifted Unit Steps
outline_section.learning_goal: Translate multiple constant pieces into a signed sum of shifted unit-step window terms.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Graph with two or more nonzero constant plateaus at different heights and at least one negative value.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Render jumps distinctly so each change in level is obvious without extra annotations.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Choose the unit-step expression that matches the piecewise constant graph with multiple level changes.
distractor_plan: Drop or merge separate intervals into one wide interval.
Assign the wrong sign for descending levels.
Use incorrect order of window endpoints.
Combine all nonzero sections into a single coefficient.
Omit one transition segment in the sum.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Convert the graph $0\to A\to B\to 0$ over two intervals to a unit-step sum.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce one shifted-window term per nonzero plateau and combine signs correctly.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Adds independent terms for multiple constant intervals beyond the single-segment case.
solution_step_plan: List all nonzero constant intervals and their heights.
Write one window term for each interval.
Scale each gate by its interval amplitude.
Sum terms and inspect interval-wise values.

outline_section.handoff_notes: This is the core multi-term assembly pattern used for most piecewise-constant graphs.

prompt_blocks.text: Choose the unit-step expression that matches the graph below.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Read the breakpoints first: the graph is 2 from 1 to 3, -1 from 3 to 5, and 3 from 5 to 7. That means one shifted window per plateau, with the plateau height attached to each window.
The other choices either merge intervals, flip the negative plateau, reverse a window order, or collapse the whole graph into one wide window. The correct sum keeps each plateau on its own interval.

prompt_blocks.text: Choose the unit-step expression that matches the graph below.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The graph is -2 from -1 to 2 and 1 from 2 to 5, so the first window is $u(t+1)$-$u(t-2)$ and the second window is $u(t-2)$-$u(t-5)$. Attach the plateau height to each window.

The wrong answers either stretch a plateau across too much time, flip the sign on the first level, reverse the step order, or drop the second plateau entirely. The correct expression matches both constant sections exactly.

prompt_blocks.text: Select the windowed expression that matches the graph.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Read each linear segment and gate it to its own interval. The rising piece is $t+1$ on $-1\le t<1$, and the falling piece is $3-t$ on $1\le t<3$, so each piece needs its own shifted-unit-step window.
